name: CyrusOne Freestone County
note: 760 MW / 506-acre campus adjacent to Calpine's Freestone Energy Center natural gas plant, ~80 miles SE of Dallas. Phase 1: 380 MW (groundbreaking June 4, 2026; online late 2026). Phase 2: additional 380 MW. Powered directly from co-located gas plant. Community concerns over economic vs. rural burden.
source: Constellation/CyrusOne press (Feb 2026); DCD; Freestone County Times; FCRecorder (Jun 2026)

name: PowerHouse Caldwell Valley
operator: PowerHouse Data Centers (American Real Estate Partners)
note: ~500-acre campus at Caldwell Valley Technology Park, a 3,600-acre master-planned site 25 miles south of Austin. PowerHouse filed to remove site from Uhland's jurisdiction and build under Caldwell County authority amid substantial resident pushback. Reclaimed water planned. No formal approval yet.
source: DCD; Baxtel; Bisnow Austin; KVUE (May 2026)

name: RB Inyokern Data Center
note: 99 MW / 238,000 sq ft AI-ready campus on 50 acres near US-395 & SR-178. 40 diesel generator sets (3 MW each) for backup power — sized just under the 100 MW CEC threshold. Developer estimates 12–16M gallons/year from the already-stressed Indian Wells Valley groundwater basin; independent estimates reach 1,822 acre-feet/year. CEC application filed April 20, 2026; 150+ public comments submitted amid strong community opposition over water, noise, and air quality.
source: California Energy Commission docket; KGET; South Kern Sol; KVPR; Roadrunner395; Somach Law (Apr–May 2026)

name: SoftBank / Foxconn Stargate Lordstown
note: SoftBank acquired former Foxconn EV plant (6.2M sq ft) at 2300 Hallock Young Rd for $375M in Aug 2025. Converting portion to AI data center hall for Stargate; remainder is AI server manufacturing JV with Foxconn. Targeted operational 2026. One of Stargate's five original U.S. sites.
source: DCD; WFMJ; TechCrunch; Tom's Hardware; Business Journal Daily (Aug 2025–2026)

name: Microsoft La Porte
note: $1B+ investment at Radius Industrial Park. First phase: 245,000 sq ft / six data centers + substation on 489 acres; a May 2026 annexation nearly tripled the site by adding ~1,200 acres, with plans for 17 buildings total. Broke ground June 17, 2026 (Vice Chair Brad Smith attended). 600+ permanent jobs. Paired with a new Microsoft Datacenter Academy at Ivy Tech Community College. Site prep began March 2026; construction through 2027; initial completion 2029.
source: Data Center Dynamics; Microsoft Local blog; ABC57; NWI Business Magazine (Jun 2026)

name: Global Stack Calistoga Fairgrounds
note: ~10 MW edge data center proposed for the city-owned Calistoga Fairgrounds, combined with a 3-story parking garage topped by a rooftop eVTOL (electric air-taxi) landing pad. Presented to the Fairgrounds Advisory Committee June 25, 2026 by Global Stack LLC, a startup founded in March 2026 pitching similar projects at 70+ California fairgrounds (including SF's Cow Palace and Solano County). Drew a packed, strongly opposed crowd over water, noise, and electricity concerns. No approval yet.
source: Data Center Dynamics; Press Democrat; KTVU; CBS San Francisco (Jun 2026)

name: Project Kilby (Chevron / Microsoft)
note: Chevron subsidiary Energy Forge One signed a 20-year behind-the-meter power agreement with Microsoft to build a co-located gas-fired power facility (~2.67 GW, phased) serving a new West Texas AI data center campus. Multibillion-dollar investment over 5–7 years; initial power targeted for 2028. Designed for minimal water use via brackish/produced water.
source: Chevron newsroom (Jun 22, 2026); Data Center Dynamics; Data Center Knowledge; Redmondmag

name: Digital Realty Astra Enterprise Park
note: Digital Realty acquired ~1,440 acres at Astra Enterprise Park for ~$475M to enter the Kansas City metro. First phase 'Astra North' (~280 acres, up to 9 buildings, ~3M sq ft) backed by an energy service agreement for 600 MW of utility power by early 2028, rising to 2 GW at full build-out.
source: Digital Realty investor release (Jun 22, 2026); Data Center Dynamics; StockTitan

name: Prime Phoenix (Avondale)
note: Broke ground May 21, 2026 on the first 3 of 5 buildings in a 66.5-acre, 240 MW, $3B+ campus (1.3M sq ft total). Buildings 1–3 already secured by a hyperscaler tenant. Uses a closed-loop cooling system engineered for zero process water use during operations.
source: Prime Data Centers newsroom; Business Wire; Data Center Dynamics (May 21, 2026)

name: OpenAI Project Camellia
note: $20–30B, 3.2 GW data center campus — four buildings across ~101 acres within the 2,600-acre Savannah Gateway Industrial Hub, 12 miles from the Port of Savannah. Georgia Power to deliver power in phases 2028–2032. Closed-loop water cooling planned to avoid diverting local water supplies. Announced Jul 22, 2026; drawn local opposition.
source: Georgia Public Broadcasting; AJC; Data Center Dynamics; TechRadar (Jul 2026)

name: Antelope Data Center
city: Iron County, UT (west of Cedar City)
note: 640-acre, ~$30B campus along Antelope Spring Road — 5 data hall buildings (~1.35M sq ft total), 1,500 MW capacity, with a dedicated on-site natural gas power station. Iron County Planning Commission approved the conditional use permit Jun 2026 after months of public hearings; no construction start confirmed yet.
source: Salt Lake Tribune; Data Center Dynamics; ABC4 Utah (Jun 2026)

name: Crusoe Callaway County
note: $4.5B, 200-acre campus off County Road 240 — two ~800,000 sq ft buildings, ~204 MW each, 500 MW campus cap. Billed as the largest private investment in county history; ~70 permanent jobs projected. Still in early planning; construction targeted fall 2026–summer 2028; county has not signed a contract yet.
source: ABC17 News; Fulton Sun; KRCG (Jun–Jul 2026)
